body: Alcobev companies make and brand spirits, beer and wine. Price is regulated state by state, and excise duties are often 60–80% of the consumer price. Profit comes from premiumisation (Prestige and Above spirits carry far higher margins than regular brands), gross margin over ENA/grain and glass, and A&P efficiency. Each state is effectively its own market with its own route to market (government corporations or private retail), price approvals and duty changes. Key metrics: volume by segment (P&A against regular), premium share of revenue, gross margin, EBITDA margin, A&P %, price increases secured from states, ENA/grain and glass costs, state concentration, and net debt (Radico's deleveraging). Cycle drivers: state excise policy (the Maharashtra 50–60% duty hike of June 2025 and MML policy; Karnataka; Andhra and Telangana route-to-market changes), grain and ENA prices (FCI rice for ethanol diverts supply), glass prices, consumer premiumisation, the India–UK FTA cutting Scotch duty, and weather for beer. Lead indicators: state excise revenue data, ISWAI commentary, maize/grain prices, CIABC releases, company P&A volume disclosures. Winners (Radico 2016–26 on premium mix and deleveraging; United Spirits after its Diageo clean-up, shedding popular brands) leaned into premiumisation, got state pricing approvals and avoided governance issues. Losers took state bans (Bihar 2016) or were stuck in regular-brand price wars and beer cost spikes. Valuation: P/E 50–90x for spirits leaders. Radico re-rated from ~18x to ~90x. Nov 2026: Radico Q2 FY27 P&A volume grew 36% to 5.28 mn cases (FY27 target raised to 30%) while total IMFL rose only 7%. United Spirits NSV grew only +2.8% on Maharashtra/Karnataka headwinds. Traps: a state policy shock, and paying 80x for premium growth.

data.business_model: Branded spirits/beer; premiumisation-led margin; state-by-state regulated pricing and route to market.
data.current_state_nov_2026: Q2 FY27: Radico P&A volume +36% to record 5.28 mn cases, FY27 P&A growth target raised to 30%, total IMFL +7%. United Spirits NSV +2.8% to ₹3,258 cr, PAT −2.1%, popular segment volumes falling, Maharashtra/Karnataka headwinds; litigation against Maharashtra MML policy. Industry shows a premium–popular divide.
data.cycle_drivers: State excise/pricing, grain/ENA prices (ethanol diversion), premiumisation, FTAs (UK Scotch), prohibition risk, weather (beer).
traps: Single-state policy shock (Maharashtra was 20–22% of USL sales)
data.valuation: Spirits leaders 50–90x P/E (Radico 18x→~90x 2016–26; USL 60–70x). Beer ~60–100x on depressed margins. Troughs: 2016 (Bihar ban, highway ban 2017).
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Grain/molasses -> ENA (distillation; backward integration helps) -> blending/bottling (glass a big cost) -> brand -> state corporation or licensed retail -> consumer. States capture the largest share via excise; premium brand owners capture most of the private margin.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: premium portfolio, backward integration in ENA, balance-sheet discipline, state-relationship management. Losers: regular-brand heavy, state concentration, governance (UB group/Mallya era), beer firms during raw-material spikes.

title: Sector playbook: Indian alcoholic beverages
